700960101.text: ...If you wanna know who's the strongest warrior, haha, look no further than our captain! He can hold back the Abyss with pure physical power alone!

700960102.text: Ha! Exactly the sort of drivel I'd expect from someone who's never seen real combat! D'you think powerful warriors just stand around hitting wooden dummies? Besides, even if we're talking raw strength, I doubt he's a match for our Grand Master...

700960103.text: Ugh, that's enough! I didn't invite you both here to listen to you bicker.

700960104.text: ...Lohen? And isn't that...Leifhelm and Slazhnev? What are you guys doing together, and what brings you two all this way from Nod-Krai?

700960105.text: Hah... I heard there were a couple of "combatologists" in Nod-Krai, so I invited them over to help me compile a "Formidable Foes Fieldbook".

700960106.text: If only I'd known combatologists were so darn combative... *sigh* Guess I'm gonna have to knock their heads together and see if I can't get them to be a bit more professional.

700960107.text: Ahaha... I—I'll start drawing up a list right away! Ehehe...

700960108.text: C—Captain Lohen! I'm not trying to be uncooperative, it's just that the word "formidable" is far too vague.

700960109.text: Never mind regular monsters — even the power gap between the Archons is huge. If we don't find a suitable benchmark, I'm afraid any further discussion will be pointless...

700960110.text: If we're talking about a benchmark of power that everyone can accept... we should probably go with dragons, right?

700960112.text: Seriously? Paimon feels like the power gaps between dragons aren't much smaller than those between the Archons...

700960115.text: Well... Long story short, after a period of reflection, I concluded that the best way to get even stronger was to challenge the most powerful opponents from all over the world.

700960116.text: (...Isn't that what you were already doing before?)

700960117.text: But then earlier this morning, just as I was about to set off... this weird-looking thing appeared in front of me and started talking a bunch of nonsense.

700960118.text: "Lost human, thrice shall you face the might of the dragon. Then, and only then, will you comprehend the true meaning of strength."

700960119.text: (That sounds like something Barbeloth would say...)

700960120.text: I'm not one for believing in prophecies, but... Hmph, well let's just say that I feel like I'm being played here, and I don't like it one bit.

700960121.text: Dragons, huh... Here in Mondstadt, you'd have to be talking about Dvalin or Ursa the Drake, or else those legends about Dragonspine... Hmm, what else is there?

700960122.text: Hah, well clearly that's where your knowledge falls short! According to top-secret intel I acquired in Nod-Krai, a powerful ancient dragon has recently snuck into Dornman Port!

700960124.text: If we want the truth, there's only one way to find out.

700960301.text: Ineffa! Ineffa! Did you see that windmill!? I need you to make a record of how it works!

700960302.text: Understood — preparing to photograph the windmill. Would you like to be included in the picture this time?

700960303.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME} and Paimon? And Lohen!? Hey there!

700960304.text: Ohhhh... Intel from Nod-Krai about a powerful ancient dragon... Paimon sees what's going on!

700960305.text: Assessing situation... It appears that Mr. Lohen hopes to fight me. Is that correct?

700960306.text: In a nutshell, yes — that's exactly what I was hoping to do. Back when the expedition was in Nod-Krai, I had no reason to suspect you had such an extraordinary history.

700960307.text: But that's all by the by. I've been wanting to test my skills against you for quite some time now, so... How about it?

700960308.text: Hehe! Ineffa, show him who's boss!

700960309.text: My apologies — according to today's schedule, we still have to visit Mondstadt to collect some special components. My assessments indicate that fighting you now may impact our subsequent operations.

700960310.text: Oh, yeah... I almost forgot! We heard there was some sort of giant robot in Mondstadt... That's why we're here! But then I got a little side-tracked...

700960312.text: Lohen... You're not seriously giving up just like that!?

700960313.text: If I help you deal with the Ruin Guards, that should clear up your schedule, right?

700960401.text: Such fluid movements... I'd never have guessed you were a machine.

700960402.text: Your attacks are also very precise, Mr. Lohen. Almost mechanically so.

700960403.text: Woohoo, new parts, hehe! I'm gonna be able to create some excellent new modules with these!

700960404.text: And... Uhm... Does this mean you're free to...

700960405.text: Ineffa, look for more! I want as many as we can get!

700960406.text: Understood... My apologies, Mr. Lohen. We can talk about this later.

700960409.text: Aino's asleep... Did she wear herself out playing in Dornman Port?

700960410.text: She's often like this — her batteries drain quickly. I am sorry, Mr. Lohen, but I'm afraid I can't get up right now. I must stay here until Aino has entered a deeper state of sleep...

700960411.text: ...That's quite all right. I've already seen enough to know what you're capable of.

700960412.text: ...I hope my combat data provides some useful insights.

700960413.text: By the way, the person who told us about these special mechanisms also mentioned Dragonspine. You might want to go there and check things out...

700960501.text: ...Seeker of Power, Follower of Fate, you are here at last.

700960502.text: It's Durin... Paimon's really not surprised at all.

700960503.text: There's something odd about the way he's speaking...

700960504.text: A sovereign ruler, the creation of a mage, and a descendant of angels... All wield disparate powers, yet all were crowned as dragons.

700960505.text: ...This is because dragons are the symbol of power.

700960506.text: So "doing battle with great dragons" became a way to prove your strength? Huh. I think I might be starting to understand the founding Grand Master a little better.

700960508.text: I can see you still have much to say, but I suggest we cross blades instead. After all, a single sword stroke is worth a thousand words!

700960509.text: W—Wait! Y—Young human, the trial you seek is far from here. You must venture to Stormterror's Lair and face the final prophecy!

700960512.text: Are you alright, Durin? You sound kinda weird today.

700960513.text: (Ahhh, phew... I think I got through the important bits... even if I did have to skip a lot!)

700960514.text: Uhm, I think Albedo said he needed help with an experiment, so I'd better be heading back now. Sorry, everyone!

700960515.text: Well he sure left in a hurry... What a shame.

700960517.text: Uhm... Why exactly was Durin here? Apart from that last line about "venturing to Stormterror's Lair," he just seemed to be talking nonsense...

subQuests.subQuestName: Seek the Dragon of the East

700960601.text: Wonderful... Now, according to Barbeloth's prophecy, the human in need of guidance should be here in no time.

700960602.text: Entrance lines... memorized. Entrance effects... confirmed. Hehe, nothing can go wrong this time!

700960603.text: Hey... Why do you guys think the "final prophecy" needs Lohen to come here?

700960604.text: Oh no, they're here already? Did Durin not finish his lines? Ugh... I need to keep quiet...

700960605.text: Could the final "might of the dragon" be talking about Dvalin? He doesn't seem to be here today, though...

700960606.text: Technically speaking, I already saw him when I first returned home from Nod-Krai. He was right beside you.

700960607.text: Oh yeah! In Wolvendom, when you were delivering letters for Varka! Wait... So does that mean the prophecy has been fulfilled already?

700960608.text: If we're being generous with our interpretation, then technically, I've already "thrice faced the might of the dragon."

700960609.text: But do you "comprehend the true meaning of strength" yet?

700960610.text: I guess that's why the prophecy has guided me here...

700960611.text: Before this place was known as Stormterror's Lair, it was the God of Storms, Decarabian's domain.

700960612.text: But the mighty god who could conjure storms to shut out the world couldn't stem the yearning for freedom within his own walls of wind.

700960613.text: Yet the God of the North Wind, with whom he had once vied for the divine throne, found the answer he had always sought only after abandoning his power.

700960614.text: Huh? There seems to be more to this kid than Varka led me to believe...

700960615.text: The Mirror of the Dawning Morn, Durin... For a time, they too were lost to confusion and doubt. What led them to strength was more than just power.

700960616.text: Well, well... You really seem to be getting it!

700960617.text: And Ursa too, the monster who had once been an angel.

700960619.text: Paimon thinks you might be on to something here, Lohen... But, uhm, you're speaking kinda funny...

700960622.text: "The angel who chose power still yearned to remain close to humanity, eventually falling to become a pitiful monster..."

700960623.text: "O humans who have witnessed this all, do you still aspire to power?"

700960626.text: Oh dear... The cat's out of the bag now, isn't it?

700960627.text: A pleasure to meet you, Lady Nicole. I've read your script, and I have to say, I was very impressed.

700960628.text: *sigh*... Why do I get the feeling that Durin dropped his copy?

700960629.text: Oh? So that was part of the prophecy, too?

700960630.text: Not at all. If I'd known in advance, I wouldn't have just... *cough*.

700960631.text: Regardless, it was a well-written script. Very entertaining — as a heartwarming little fairy tale, of course. I must say though, I'm not a huge fan of being lectured to... not even by an angel.

700960632.text: ...I'll choose to believe that was aimed at my former colleague — the one who chose power.

700960633.text: Seeing as you've read my script, I suppose you already know everything I have to say?

700960634.text: Indeed, and I'll make sure to treat it as valued advice. Now, was there anything else — or can I get back to compiling my Formidable Foes Fieldbook?

700960201.text: Our captain isn't just strong — he even developed a compound that counters the Abyss! Bet you didn't know that, did you, smartypants? And yet you think I'm a "false expert" who doesn't know anything!?

700960202.text: Well, do you know about our Grand Master's amazing speed? He used the Ley Lines to travel all the way from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt in less time than it takes you to tie your shoelaces — if you even know how!

700960701.text: *sigh* Still, even if it was my first attempt, I can't believe this is how things turned out...

700960703.text: Besides, it didn't really end badly!

700960705.text: Hah... My first Witch's Homework. I'll explain it all later.
